repositories.name: reel
repositories.description: Record your terminal once and let your agent edit it into a polished demo in seconds 📼

paragraphs: Record a terminal session once, then treat it as a timeline you can cut, speed-ramp, zoom, caption, restyle, and score with sound — re-rendering in milliseconds without ever re-running the underlying program.

Plenty of tools will get a terminal session onto disk and back out as pixels. reel is about the half that comes after: post-production. The recording is frozen; the edit is a text file you keep changing.
A real Claude Code session, recorded once and then cut, annotated, speed-ramped and scored by reel — from one edit script. The WebM carries procedural sound; GIF can't.

repositories.name: LiteRT-Models
repositories.description: Converted TFLite Model Zoo for Android with LiteRT CompiledModel GPU acceleration

paragraphs: LiteRT is Google's on-device ML runtime for Android and the successor to TensorFlow Lite (renamed 2024-09): PyTorch models are converted with Google's litert-torch into .tflite files that run every op on the phone's GPU through CompiledModel (ML Drift), e.g. DINOv2 ViT-S/14 at 448² runs in 53.6 ms on a Galaxy S26 GPU (npubench, LiteRT 2.2.0, median of 50 runs, 2026-08).

This repository is the model zoo for that path: 91 converted models (as of 2026-09-08), each with its download, input/output shapes, preprocessing, the conversion script that produced it, and a standalone Android sample app (Kotlin). No MediaPipe and no vendor SDK: the .tflite graphs run on CompiledModel GPU with every op delegated (no CPU fallback), and the four 3B chat models run on LiteRT-LM. The GPU-compatibility rewrites these conversions need are catalogued in docs/LITERTCONVERSIONGUIDE.md and packaged in litertgputoolkit/.
If you like this repository, please give it a star.
